paper_title: Searching for axion-like particles with ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions
notes: Paper presents projected sensitivity of ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions to ALP-photon coupling 1/Lambda (GeV^-1) and new/updated LEP/LHC recast limits. Coupling is the ALP-photon (aFF) coupling 1/Lambda, related to g_agamma. However, the y-axis is given as 1/Lambda in GeV^-1 (note g_agamma = 1/Lambda with the Lagrangian normalization used), and all numerical values are only available from Fig. 4 which is not extractable as a table. Mass range ~5-100 GeV. No specific numerical (mass, coupling) pairs could be reliably extracted from the text. Not a DM haloscope, so no DM density. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 4 left panel (aFF̃ coupling). Y-axis is 1/Λ in GeV⁻¹, proportional to g_aγγ (g_aγγ = 1/Λ for this normalization convention, but note Eq.1 uses 1/4 a/Λ F F̃). Traced the green solid curve = projected Pb-Pb 1 nb⁻¹ sensitivity, which is the main new result. X-axis is hybrid: log below 5 GeV, linear above 5 GeV. Only the linear region (5-100 GeV) is reliably traced. The dashed green curve (10 nb⁻¹) lies lower but the solid 1 nb⁻¹ curve is the nominal current-luminosity sensitivity. Existing constraints (OPAL, ATLAS, CMS, Beam Dump) sit at higher coupling values.
